items.name: Professionals & employees trained in data and AI-related skills
items.definition: Individuals resident in Rwanda who completed a recognised training programme in data science, machine learning or applied AI during the reference year.
items.methodology: Compiled from provider and programme reporting. Boundary conditions, minimum contact hours, deduplication of repeat attendees, are not standardised across providers, which is why the indicator carries an estimated evidence type.

items.name: New jobs created requiring data and AI skills
items.definition: Jobs created during the reference year whose stated requirements include data or AI skills.
items.methodology: Derived from labour-market and platform postings. Counts advertised roles rather than filled positions.

items.name: Companies using data and AI-related skills
items.definition: Firms operating in Rwanda that report using data or AI-related skills in their operations.
items.methodology: Self-reported through industry surveys and member returns. Definitions of 'using AI' vary by respondent.

items.name: AI meetups and participants
items.definition: AI-focused meetups and community events held in Rwanda during the reference year.
items.methodology: Event listings and organiser returns. A proxy for the informal learning sector outside universities.

items.name: Science graduates per capita
items.definition: Science graduates per head of population.
items.methodology: UNESCO UIS graduate counts divided by the NISR mid-year population estimate. Used as a proxy for the pipeline feeding technical fields.

items.name: Citations of AI papers authored from Rwanda
items.definition: Citations accruing to AI-related papers with at least one Rwanda-affiliated author.
items.methodology: Scimago country and subject-area extraction. Citation counts lag publication by two to three years.

items.name: Deep learning papers
items.definition: Deep-learning papers with at least one Rwanda-affiliated author.
items.methodology: Bibliometric extraction on subject classification. Preprints and conference papers are included.

items.name: Research funding secured for AI and data science
items.note: Code collision with RWA2-SUBb in the source framework; resolved at digitisation.
items.definition: Research funding secured by Rwandan institutions specifically for AI and data-science work.
items.methodology: Institutional reporting. Multi-year grants are recognised in the year of award, not spread across the term.

items.name: Post-graduates from AI & data science courses
items.definition: Students graduating from postgraduate AI and data-science programmes in the reference year.
items.methodology: Higher-education administrative records across the institutions offering such programmes.

items.name: Researchers in AI / STEM
items.definition: Researchers working in AI, or in STEM where an AI-specific figure is unavailable.
items.methodology: UNESCO UIS researcher headcount. The AI-specific share is not separately published.

items.name: Universities offering AI and data science degrees
items.definition: Universities offering a degree programme in AI or data science.
items.methodology: Count of accredited programmes. Short courses and certificates are excluded.

items.name: Collaboration programmes with foreign universities
items.definition: Active collaboration programmes between Rwandan and foreign universities involving AI or data science.
items.methodology: Includes co-authored research programmes, MOOCs, exchange programmes and satellite campuses, as tracked by OECD collaboration data.

items.name: Schools offering AI and technology skills
items.note: Code collision with RWA2.2 in the source framework; resolved at digitisation.
items.definition: Primary and secondary schools offering formal AI or technology instruction.
items.methodology: Ministry administrative records. The 2022 assessment found only one school meeting the definition, and noted that teaching may occur without being reported.

items.name: STEM graduates per capita
items.definition: Students graduating from STEM programmes per head of population.
items.methodology: UNESCO UIS graduate counts over the NISR population estimate.

items.name: R software package downloads
items.definition: Downloads of R statistical packages attributed to Rwanda.
items.methodology: Cranlogs download counts. A proxy for applied analytics activity; attribution by IP is imperfect.

items.name: AI patents filed by Rwandan applicants
items.definition: Patent applications with an AI classification filed by Rwandan applicants.
items.methodology: Registrar General and WIPO filings under AI-related classification codes.

items.name: International students in AI-related programmes
items.definition: International students enrolled in Rwandan university programmes that include AI content.
items.methodology: Institutional enrolment records.

items.name: Collaborators on open-source AI packages
items.definition: Distinct contributors from Rwanda to open-source AI packages.
items.methodology: GitHub public activity filtered to AI package repositories. Country attribution relies on self-declared profile location.

items.name: Commits on open-source AI packages
items.definition: Commits from Rwanda to open-source AI packages during the reference year.
items.methodology: GitHub public activity. Captures all contribution types, so it overstates AI-specific work and understates private contribution.

items.name: Average commits per collaborator
items.definition: Average commits per Rwandan contributor to open-source AI packages.
items.methodology: TOR92 divided by TOR88. Sensitive to small numbers of contributors.

items.name: Visa processing time for skilled workers
items.definition: Working days to process an entry visa for a skilled worker.
items.methodology: Immigration service published service standard. Lower is better, so the goalposts are inverted.

items.name: Change in cost of cloud resources (IaaS basket)
items.definition: Percentage change in the cost of a fixed basket of cloud infrastructure resources, in Rwandan francs.
items.methodology: A fixed IaaS or storage basket priced across authorised vendors. Falling cost scores higher, so the goalposts are inverted.

items.name: International cloud providers registered & authorised
items.note: Source corrected from UNESCO to the RURA authorisation register at digitisation.
items.definition: International cloud service providers registered and authorised to store and process data in Rwanda.
items.methodology: RURA authorisation register. The 2022 assessment recorded zero; authorisation is a precondition for regulated workloads.

items.name: Companies using authorised cloud services
items.note: Source corrected from Cranlogs at digitisation.
items.definition: Firms using an authorised cloud service.
items.methodology: Regulatory returns from authorised providers.

items.name: Average fixed download speed
items.definition: Median fixed broadband download speed.
items.methodology: Ookla Speedtest Global Index monthly median for Rwanda.

items.name: Population with access to electricity
items.definition: Share of the population with access to electricity.
items.methodology: World Bank development indicators.

items.name: Internet users as a share of adults
items.definition: Internet users as a share of the adult population.
items.methodology: World Bank and GSMA connectivity data. The 2022 assessment recorded 27 percent against a world average of 63 percent.

items.name: 4G population coverage
items.definition: Share of the population covered by a 4G mobile signal.
items.methodology: Regulatory coverage returns. Coverage is not the same as use, see mobile internet use.

items.name: Global Cybersecurity Index
items.definition: ITU Global Cybersecurity Index score.
items.methodology: Published composite covering legal, technical, organisational, capacity-building and cooperation measures. Ingested as published and never recomputed.

items.name: Blueprint for a continental AI-ready hyperscale data centre
items.note: Three-state partial credit applied in methodology v1.2.
items.definition: Stage reached in preparing a blueprint for a continental AI-ready hyperscale data centre.
items.methodology: Three-state ordinal: not in place, drafted, in force.

items.name: Data centres / local compute capacity established
items.definition: Data centres or local compute facilities established and operating in Rwanda.
items.methodology: Includes the national data centre and commercial facilities. Counts facilities, not capacity.

items.name: Companies in the cloud computing value chain
items.note: De-duplicated at digitisation.
items.definition: Firms providing products or services in the cloud computing value chain.
items.methodology: Company register filtered to relevant activity classifications.

items.name: People employed in the cloud value chain
items.definition: People employed in the cloud computing value chain.
items.methodology: Employer returns and industry estimates.

items.name: National accelerated-compute capacity for researchers
items.note: Proposed v1.2 addition, not in the 2022 framework.
items.definition: Accelerated compute capacity, in PFLOP/s, available to Rwandan researchers and firms.
items.methodology: Declared capacity of national and institutional GPU resources. Proposed in methodology v1.2; the 2026 landscape review records no domestic frontier capacity.

items.name: Open government data (ODIN)
items.definition: Open Data Inventory score for the coverage and openness of official statistics.
items.methodology: Published by Open Data Watch. Ingested as published.

items.name: Statistical capacity score
items.definition: World Bank statistical capacity score.
items.methodology: Composite of statistical methodology, data sources and periodicity. The 2022 assessment recorded 73, above the sub-Saharan African average.

items.name: Published data collection, storage and sharing protocols
items.definition: Stage reached in publishing frameworks and protocols for data collection, storage, processing and sharing.
items.methodology: Three-state ordinal: not in place, drafted, in force.

items.name: Data sources available via the national sharing platform
items.definition: Datasets discoverable and accessible through the national data-sharing platform.
items.methodology: Platform catalogue count. Availability is not the same as usability for model training.

items.name: Rwanda-specific annotated datasets released
items.definition: Rwanda-specific annotated datasets released for public use.
items.methodology: Counts released, documented and licensed datasets. The 2022 assessment recorded two.

items.name: AI-ready datasets available and used
items.definition: Annotated datasets in active use for model training or evaluation.
items.methodology: A subset of released datasets, confirmed as used by at least one project.

items.name: Government has a dedicated AI governmental body
items.definition: Whether government has a dedicated body responsible for AI.
items.methodology: Binary. Satisfied by an office or agency with an explicit AI mandate.

items.name: National AI policy / strategy in force
items.definition: Whether a national AI policy or strategy is formally in force.
items.methodology: Binary. Rwanda adopted the first national AI policy in Africa in 2023.

items.name: Dedicated public spending line on AI
items.definition: Whether a dedicated public spending line for AI exists in the budget.
items.methodology: Binary, assessed against published budget documents.

items.name: Level of data protection regulation
items.definition: Level of data protection regulation in force.
items.methodology: UNCTAD cyberlaw tracker, mapped to an ordinal scale. Rwanda's law became enforceable in 2023.

items.name: Civil servants trained (regulators, policymakers, legislators)
items.definition: Civil servants who have completed AI policy or regulatory training.
items.methodology: Programme records, prioritising regulators, policymakers and legislators.

items.name: Partnerships for regulator training
items.definition: Partnerships with international agencies delivering AI training to Rwandan regulators.
items.methodology: Institutional agreements in force during the reference year.

items.name: Regulators participating in AI training
items.definition: Regulators who have participated in AI training programmes.
items.methodology: Programme attendance records.

items.name: Position in a global AI readiness index
items.note: Rank inverted over a 172-country field.
items.definition: Rwanda's position in a globally recognised government AI readiness index.
items.methodology: Oxford Insights Government AI Readiness Index. Scored by rank inversion over the 172-country field; edition changes affect comparability.

items.name: Participation in the ISO AI committee
items.definition: Level of participation in ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42, the international AI standards committee.
items.methodology: Ordinal: none, observer, participating member.

items.name: Signatory of the Open Data Charter
items.definition: Whether Rwanda is a signatory to the International Open Data Charter.
items.methodology: Binary, from the Charter's published membership.

items.name: AI solutions adopted in government / public value chains
items.definition: AI solutions in production use within government or public value chains.
items.methodology: Counted from the use-case registry. Only deployments past pilot stage are included.

items.name: Government agencies adopting AI
items.definition: Government agencies operating at least one AI solution in production.
items.methodology: Distinct institutions in the use-case registry.

items.name: AI solutions deployed in the Rwandan market
items.definition: AI solutions deployed commercially in the Rwandan market.
items.methodology: Use-case registry entries from private-sector providers in production or scaled stages.

items.name: Volume of AI investment (VC, institutional, public)
items.definition: Disclosed investment into Rwandan AI activity from venture, institutional, philanthropic and public sources.
items.methodology: Aggregated from funding databases and partnership announcements. Undisclosed rounds are excluded, so the figure is a floor.

items.name: Local companies investing in AI capabilities
items.definition: Rwandan companies making disclosed investment in their own AI capability.
items.methodology: Company reporting and survey returns.

items.name: Sector-specific AI deployment plans implemented
items.definition: Stage reached in implementing sector-specific AI deployment plans.
items.methodology: Three-state ordinal: not in place, drafted, in force.

items.name: Proof-of-concept projects under PPP
items.definition: Proof-of-concept AI projects running under a public–private partnership.
items.methodology: Use-case registry entries at proof-of-concept or pilot stage with both a public and a private party.

items.name: Government has publicly dedicated money to AI
items.definition: Whether government has publicly dedicated money to AI.
items.methodology: Binary, assessed against published budget and programme documents.

items.name: Local–international firm collaborations on AI projects
items.definition: Collaborations between Rwandan and international firms delivering national AI projects.
items.methodology: Contract and partnership records.

items.name: R&D spending as a share of GDP
items.definition: Gross domestic expenditure on research and development as a share of GDP.
items.methodology: UNESCO UIS. The AI-attributable share is not separately measured anywhere.

items.name: AI companies per 100,000 population
items.note: Decomposed from the compound indicator OXF12.
items.definition: AI companies per 100,000 population.
items.methodology: Company database counts over the NISR population estimate. Coverage of African firms in commercial databases is partial.

items.name: AI start-ups per 100,000 population
items.note: Decomposed from the compound indicator OXF12.
items.definition: AI start-ups per 100,000 population.
items.methodology: As above, restricted to firms under the database's start-up classification.

items.name: Public–private partnership AI projects
items.definition: Public–private partnership projects delivering AI solutions.
items.methodology: Use-case registry entries with both a public and a private party.

items.name: Accreditation programme for innovative tech companies
items.definition: Stage reached in launching an accreditation programme for innovative technology companies.
items.methodology: Three-state ordinal: not in place, drafted, in force.

items.name: Regulatory sandbox platform launched
items.definition: Stage reached in launching a regulatory sandbox for AI and data-driven services.
items.methodology: Three-state ordinal: not in place, drafted, in force.

items.name: Sandbox uptake (actors, matches, dataset downloads)
items.definition: Uptake of the regulatory sandbox, counting participating actors, matches made and dataset downloads.
items.methodology: Sandbox operator reporting.

items.name: National AI ethics framework published
items.note: Partial credit: drafted and pending board approval scores 50.
items.definition: Stage reached in publishing a national AI ethics framework.
items.methodology: Three-state ordinal. Rwanda's framework was developed in 2022 and remains pending board approval, which scores 50.

items.name: Organisations endorsing the ethics guidelines
items.definition: Organisations that have formally endorsed the national AI ethics guidelines.
items.methodology: Endorsement register.

items.name: AI Ethics Officers appointed
items.definition: AI ethics officers appointed across public and private organisations.
items.methodology: Institutional returns.

items.name: Stakeholders in industry consultation
items.definition: Stakeholders participating in the national AI ethics industry consultation.
items.methodology: Consultation attendance records.

items.name: AI and Democratic Values Index
items.definition: Artificial Intelligence and Democratic Values Index score.
items.methodology: Published index scoring national commitments on AI and democratic values. Ingested as published.

items.name: MOUs with other regulatory agencies
items.definition: Memoranda of understanding signed and implemented with other regulatory agencies on AI matters.
items.methodology: Regulator records. Counts implemented agreements, not signed-only.

items.name: International / regional AI platforms Rwanda belongs to
items.definition: International or regional AI platforms in which Rwanda holds formal membership.
items.methodology: Membership records of standards bodies, policy networks and continental initiatives.

items.name: Measured frontier AI usage index
items.note: Proxy measure. Covers one provider, so it understates total frontier AI use by an unknown margin.
items.definition: Observed frontier AI usage relative to the level expected for an economy of Rwanda's size and working-age population, where 1.00 is the expected value.
items.methodology: Anthropic Economic Index country view. Usage is measured from Claude.ai conversations only and is a proxy for frontier AI adoption.

items.name: Global rank on measured AI usage
items.definition: Rwanda's position among 121 ranked economies on measured frontier AI usage.
items.methodology: Rank inverted over the 121-economy field for scoring.

items.name: Human Capital Index
items.note: Below the sub-Saharan African average and marginally above the low-income group average. AI literacy is being built on top of this.
items.definition: Expected productivity in adulthood of a child born today, relative to complete education and full health.
items.methodology: World Bank Human Capital Index, 0 to 1. Most recent published value is 2020.

items.name: Harmonised learning outcome score
items.definition: Harmonised test score on a scale running from 300 at minimum attainment to 625 at advanced attainment.
items.methodology: World Bank harmonised learning outcomes, component of the Human Capital Index.

items.name: Teachers reached by national AI literacy programmes
items.note: Neither the general workforce nor the informal sector is covered by any current instrument.
items.definition: Cumulative teachers reached by national AI literacy and awareness programmes.
items.methodology: Programme reporting compiled in the 2026 landscape review.

items.name: Public institutions covered by AI capacity programmes
items.definition: Public institutions whose staff have been reached by national AI capacity building.
items.methodology: Programme reporting compiled in the 2026 landscape review.

items.name: Smartphone ownership
items.note: Handsets average around USD 160. Device cost is a primary driver of the measured usage gap.
items.definition: Share of the population owning a smartphone.
items.methodology: Sector reporting cited in the 2026 landscape review.

items.name: Mobile internet use
items.definition: Share of the population actively using mobile internet.
items.methodology: Sector reporting cited in the 2026 landscape review.

items.name: National installed electricity generation
items.note: A single hyperscale AI campus draws over 100 MW. The energy envelope, not capital, is the binding constraint on sovereign frontier compute.
items.definition: Installed national generating capacity available to the grid.
items.methodology: Indicative national figures from grid operator and sector reporting, 2022 to 2023, pending updated publication.

items.name: External AI-specific financial commitments
items.note: Concentrated: two of the largest commitments come from one foundation and both concentrate in health.
items.definition: Cumulative externally committed funding specifically earmarked for AI programmes in Rwanda since 2025.
items.methodology: Sum of disclosed partnership commitments: Horizon 1000 (USD 50m), AI Scaling Hub (USD 17.5m) and TAIRI Lab (USD 0.54m).

items.name: Africa AI Governance Index score
items.definition: Continental assessment of capacity to govern AI, scored out of 4 across strategy and implementation.
items.methodology: Published index. Rwanda is the only state scoring strongly on both strategy and implementation.

items.name: Global AI Readiness Index rank
items.definition: Rwanda's position among 195 economies on readiness to deploy AI.
items.methodology: Rank inverted over the 195-economy field for scoring. Measures readiness to build, not capacity to govern.

items.name: Openly licensed Rwandan language models released
items.note: The only genuinely sovereign layer of Rwanda's AI stack.
items.definition: Sovereign, openly licensed Kinyarwanda language and speech models released for public use.
items.methodology: Count of released models: KinyaBERT, KinyaColBERT and Flex-TTS, released open source in March 2026.

items.name: AI-specific legislation in force
items.note: Confirmed absent by the government's own catalogue. The Policy & Responsible AI pillar lists under What Exists Today only Rwanda's data protection and cybersecurity legal framework. No AI statute is claimed.
items.definition: Whether Rwanda has enacted legislation specific to artificial intelligence.
items.methodology: Binary assessment. Enforcement currently rests on the data protection regime alone.

items.name: Public register of state AI systems
items.note: Raised from 0 to 50 on 17 September 2026. RAIA's national record at ai.gov.rw/record publishes 34 verified use cases across 43 institutions, dated and reviewed against primary documentation. It is an investment catalogue rather than an accountability register: it carries sector and stage, not risk classification, oversight arrangements or routes to redress. Rwanda now publishes what it deploys, but not how those systems are governed.
items.definition: Whether a public register of AI systems used by the state is published, covering the deploying institution, the model, the legal basis, a risk classification, the human oversight arrangement and the route to redress.
items.methodology: Ordinal. 0 none; 50 a public inventory exists but without risk, oversight or redress metadata; 100 a transparency register meeting the full definition.

items.name: National model evaluation capability
items.note: The Health Intelligence Centre contains the only formally resourced model evaluation function in the country. Confirmed absent by the government's own catalogue. The Policy & Responsible AI pillar lists under What Needs To Be Built: model assurance and AI testing and evaluation capability, tools and institutions that verify AI systems before and during deployment.
items.definition: Whether a national capability exists to independently evaluate AI model performance and safety.
items.methodology: Binary assessment. Vendor accuracy claims currently have no domestic verifier.

items.name: AI procurement standard with continuity and exit terms
items.note: Rwanda's largest digital health deployment reached close to a fifth of the population and collapsed in 2023 when its foreign parent entered bankruptcy. Not claimed anywhere in the government's own catalogue. The Financing & Partnerships pillar lists outcome-based payment-verification machinery as still to be built.
items.definition: Whether a national AI procurement standard exists covering continuity, data portability and exit.
items.methodology: Binary assessment. The state is anchor buyer without continuity or exit terms.

items.name: National term on ownership of fine-tuned models
items.note: The cheapest of the identified gaps to close and, on the review's assessment, the most valuable to Rwanda's position in the value chain.
items.definition: Whether a standard national contractual term defines ownership of models fine-tuned on Rwandan public data.
items.methodology: Binary assessment.

items.name: Standalone national AI agency established
items.definition: Whether a dedicated standalone national AI institution exists, distinct from an office inside a ministry.
items.methodology: Binary assessment. Approved by Cabinet on 8 June 2026; Africa's first standalone national AI institution.

items.name: National fibre optic network deployed
items.definition: Kilometres of national fibre optic backbone deployed.
items.methodology: Self-reported by RAIA in the national AI catalogue. The measurement date and whether the figure counts backbone only or includes last-mile distribution are not published.

items.name: Digital identity coverage
items.definition: Share of the population holding a digital identity, the identity rail on which trusted data services depend.
items.methodology: RAIA's catalogue states near-universal coverage without a figure. Recorded here as 95% pending a published number, and flagged in_review for that reason.

items.name: STEM graduates per year
items.definition: Graduates completing STEM programmes in the reference year, counted in absolute terms.
items.methodology: Self-reported by RAIA. Held alongside the per-capita indicators OXF20 and TOR36, which remain the internationally comparable form.

items.name: Government officials reached by AI training
items.note: Held separately from RWA8 (civil servants completing AI policy or regulatory training, 41 in the 2022 assessment) and from the 2026 review's figure of 50 officials across 24 institutions. The three differ by orders of magnitude and almost certainly measure different depths of training. The platform publishes all three rather than choosing between them, see the Talent view.
items.definition: Cumulative government officials recorded as having received AI training of any depth, as reported by RAIA.
items.methodology: Self-reported by RAIA in the national AI catalogue. The programme definition, contact hours and deduplication basis are not published.

items.name: Sovereign GPUs available to national workloads
items.note: No observation is recorded because none is published. The indicator is declared so the gap is visible and counts against coverage.
items.definition: Graphics processing units under sovereign control and available to government, university and startup workloads.
items.methodology: Unit and target taken from RAIA's compute pillar, which states an ambition of 24 to 48 or more sovereign GPUs by 2028. No current figure is published.

items.name: AI-ready public datasets published
items.note: Declared without an observation. RAIA's data pillar lists the National Data Hub itself as still to be built, so a published count is not expected yet.
items.definition: Government datasets prepared to an AI-ready standard: secure, documented and interoperable.
items.methodology: Target of 100 or more taken from RAIA's data pillar, which states this as a national ambition. No current count is published.
